clue.text: International group genuinely leaderless and out of control

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a group of nations

indicators.note: a word without its leader has lost its first letter, so the opening letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: genuinely means truly

explanation.surface: A global body that is truly headless and running amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the T from TRULY, leaving RULY. The puzzle's theme is words whose positive forms (ruly, couth, gainly) are rarely used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unruly describes people or things that refuse discipline, which is being out of control.

clue.text: Clumsy French article widely misinterpreted

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, 'a'

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so these letters are taken in a different order

explanation.surface: A clumsy French article has been widely misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' is the anagram signal; 'French article' is the French for 'a', not a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwieldy is awkward to handle, so it is clumsy in use.

clue.text: Socialist message, like the words of Jesus?

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist
a letter is a written message

explanation.surface: A leftist's communication compared to the sayings of Christ.
explanation.walkthrough: Many Bibles print Christ's words in red ink, so they are literally red-letter text.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-letter Bibles print the sayings of Jesus in red, so his words are red-letter words.

clue.text: To Schubert, a song told a story

definitions.meaning: The German word for a song, the form Schubert wrote hundreds of
told an untruth, a story in the sense of a fib

explanation.surface: Schubert's song was a narrative piece.
explanation.definitionFit: German art songs are called Lieder, singular Lied; and telling stories is a polite way of saying fibbing.

clue.text: Not making a profit, perhaps? Awkward

definitions.meaning: read playfully as ..., in a manner without gain

explanation.surface: A loss-making firm is an embarrassing thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer into UN, GAIN and LY: acting without gain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungainly person moves without grace, which is being awkward.

clue.text: It makes you sick seeing North America exploit worker

parts.note: to exploit is to use
a worker is a type of ant, hence the crossword staple ANT

explanation.surface: Seeing America exploit its labourers is sickening.
explanation.definitionFit: A nauseant is a substance that induces nausea, an agent that makes one feel sick.

clue.text: People in solitary confinement? Turkish city-dwellers, some say

indicators.note: some say signals that the answer is how certain people pronounce the clue's phrase

parts.note: residents of Ankara, the Turkish capital, might be called Ankara-ites

explanation.surface: Prisoners in isolation might be Turkish urbanites, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some say' tells us the answer sounds like Ankara-ites, people of Ankara, at least in some accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchorites are religious recluses who shut themselves away in a cell, a voluntary solitary confinement.

clue.text: Island's gold found in capsized vessel

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue a capsized thing is upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Treasure is discovered in an overturned boat off an island.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'capsized' turns the vessel upside down, and 'found in' places the gold. Island's reads as 'Island is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: One most revered? Question of motive raised about article he brought up

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: asking why is questioning someone's motive
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means the word rises, read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Asking about motives regarding something a man mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns WHY into YHW, which goes 'about' A to give YAHW; 'brought up' turns HE into EH.
explanation.definitionFit: Yahweh is the Hebrew name for God, the being most revered in Judaism.

clue.text: Turn around, very unwelcome still

indicators.note: an unwelcome thing is not let in, so this letter is shut out of the word

parts.note: to invert is to turn upside down or around

explanation.surface: Turning round, someone stays motionless and decidedly unwanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwelcome' removes V from INVERT. 'still' is the definition, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or inactive, so still in the sense of not moving.

clue.text: One duck winged around, circling another

indicators.note: circling says the anagrammed letters go round the other piece
around suggests letters thrown about and rearranged

parts.note: another duck: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck flies around, wheeling about another bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges WINGED, and those letters go 'circling' O, the cricketing duck or zero score.
explanation.definitionFit: The widgeon (also wigeon) is a species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Ploughman's perhaps wiping mouth, eating out with no manners

indicators.note: eating says one piece swallows the other
the mouth is the opening, so wiping it removes the word's first letter

parts.note: a ploughman's is a British pub lunch of bread, cheese and pickle

explanation.surface: Someone eats a pub lunch out without wiping their mouth, showing no manners.
explanation.walkthrough: A ploughman's lunch is a British pub meal. 'wiping mouth' drops L from LUNCH; UNCH is 'eating' OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth means lacking refinement or politeness, being without manners.

clue.text: The first girlfriend, right as always

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, Adam's partner in Genesis

explanation.surface: A first girlfriend is right, as she always is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, the same as always, as in 'ever faithful'.

clue.text: Flip-flopping Tories rule badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservative governments that dither make for poor rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TORIES RULE; the definition comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip-flopping politician keeps changing position, which is being undecided or irresolute.

clue.text: Dreadful day, resulting in upset

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A terrible day ends with someone feeling upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges RESULTING into ISGRUNTLE, after D for day. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgruntle someone is to make them discontented, to upset or annoy them.

clue.text: Endless delay with large catalogue

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to detain someone is to delay them
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Interminable hold-ups with a big list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims the synonym for delay, not the word 'delay' itself; 'catalogue' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail things is to list them item by item, which is to catalogue them.

clue.text: Cool drink setter had in flat

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
to sip is to drink
the setter is 'I', so setter had is I'd

explanation.surface: The setter had a cool drink in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like a home in the surface but is an adjective meaning dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid means lacking flavour or interest; flat is a synonym for something dull and lifeless.

clue.text: Those who are stupid as I live in foreign climes

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the other
foreign suggests something strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Fools, like me, dwell in faraway lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges I with CLIMES to give IMCILES, and 'in' places the synonym for live after the M. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbeciles is an insulting term for fools, people thought to be stupid.

clue.text: One of the sides of gym's not as dim

parts.words: One of the sides of gym's
parts.note: the sides of gym are G and M, so one of them is 'G or M'
less means not as much, as in 'not as' in a comparison

explanation.surface: One side of the gymnasium is not as dimly lit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, one of the sides of 'gym' is 'G OR M'; 'not as' gives LESS. Gorm is also a back-formation in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is a British word for stupid or slow-witted, which is dim.

clue.text: Pessimistic, no?

definitions.meaning: a reply meaning no; the question mark flags this sense

explanation.definitionFit: A negative outlook is a gloomy one, and 'no' is the negative answer to a question.

clue.text: Bore and thug taking advantage of the same good cavalryman

parts.note: a drag is a tedious thing, a bore

indicators.note: the second word uses the same G already ending the first, so its own copy is dropped

parts.note: a goon is a thug

explanation.surface: A dull ruffian exploiting the same goods as a soldier on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAG and GOON share one G: 'taking advantage of the same good' drops GOON's own G, leaving OON.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantryman, a type of cavalry soldier.

clue.text: Wishy-washy, but offered bolder ingredients occasionally

indicators.note: some of the letters, taken every other one, form the answer's ingredients

explanation.surface: A bland dish despite offering stronger ingredients now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredients occasionally' takes the even letters of OFFERED BOLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishy-washy means weak or lacking strength of character, as does feeble.

clue.text: Admirer, they say, supporting soldiers someone abandoned

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting places the piece underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: they say means the word is given as heard, so the sound is kept and the spelling changes

parts.note: a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A fan, so people say, backing troops who have been left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' gives FAN as it sounds, PHAN; it goes 'supporting', below, OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphan is a child left without parents, sometimes literally a foundling abandoned by them.

clue.text: Clumsy writer from the South defined by sex

indicators.note: defined by means bounded, so this piece encloses the other

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'

indicators.note: in a down entry, from the South means read upwards from the bottom

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward author from the south, known for their sex life.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'from the South' reads the writer upwards; 'defined by' means enclosed by. IT as sex is a coy old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, a near synonym for clumsy or bungling.

clue.text: Recovery of space in defective computer

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other
defective suggests broken, so the word's letters are reassembled

parts.note: an en is a unit of space in printing

explanation.surface: Retrieving storage space from a broken PC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defective' rearranges COMPUTER, and EN, the printer's space, goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recoupment is the act of recovering money lost or spent, a recovery.

clue.text: Bishop is at first trapped in toilet in passenger section of plane; …

indicators.note: trapped in means the pieces are held inside another

parts.note: can is American slang for a toilet
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A bishop gets stuck in the lavatory on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: B and I, the first of 'is', are 'trapped in' CAN. The ellipsis carries the bishop into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabin is the part of an aircraft where passengers sit.

clue.text: Official record secreted in Cluniac tabernacle

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away, so the answer is concealed within these words

explanation.surface: Formal minutes tucked away in a monastery's tabernacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secreted in' hides the answer across Cluniac tabernacle; the Cluniacs were a Benedictine order.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta are official proceedings or acts of a body, written down as its formal record.

clue.text: … supporter of cathedral gets him a promotion

definitions.meaning: a structural support in a cathedral
him is the bishop of the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continuing from the bishop, someone backing the cathedral wins advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue's bishop: ARCH before bishop gives archbishop, a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Arches bear the weight of a cathedral's vaults, and an archbishop outranks a bishop.

clue.text: Regular, somewhat boring colour

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a hue is a colour
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: A usual, rather dull shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it puts A BIT inside HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular visitor to a place, as in a pub's regulars.

clue.text: I'll drive on the right and tear around in this brand of tyre

indicators.note: around means turned back to front, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: on the right picks the letter at the right-hand end of the following word

parts.note: to rip is to tear

explanation.surface: A boast about driving fast on the right, ripping round on these tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the right' takes only the end of 'drive'; the joined letters ILLERIP are read backwards because of 'around'. The apostrophe in I'll is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirelli is an Italian company famous for making tyres, a well-known tyre brand.

clue.text: New Age philosophy according to some: a sort of oneness with nature, primarily

definitions.text: New Age philosophy according to some

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken
a sort of signals a version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some say New Age thinking is mainly about feeling one with the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sort of' rearranges ONENESS, after N, the first of 'nature'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptics dismiss New Age beliefs as rubbish, which is what nonsense means.

clue.text: Pure and mostly humble

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to chasten someone is to humble them

explanation.surface: Innocent and largely modest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter, N, from CHASTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means sexually virtuous or innocent, which is pure.
